title: Ireland – Design consultancy services – Request for Tender for the Provision of a Shared Island Media Fund Talent Development and Content Development Initiative for Audiovisual Content
description: The Commission is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified service provider for the design, management and delivery of a Shared Island Media Fund Talent Development and Content Development Initiative for Audiovisual Content. The successful Tenderer will be required to design, manage and deliver a structured programme of talent development and content development activities that strengthen professional capability within the audiovisual sector, facilitate collaboration between practitioners across the island of Ireland and support the development of high-quality audiovisual projects aligned with the objectives of the Shared Island Media Fund. The services to be provided include, but are not limited to: • designing and delivering a structured programme of workshops, masterclasses, mentoring, networking events and audiovisual content development activities; • developing and implementing a fair, open and transparent recruitment and selection process for programme participants; • facilitating collaboration between audiovisual practitioners from across the island of Ireland, including participants from different jurisdictions, backgrounds and communities; • providing experienced facilitators, mentors and industry specialists to support participant learning and project development; • supporting participants in the development of audiovisual projects that demonstrate potential to progress to production and reflect the objectives of the Shared Island Media Fund; • managing all aspects of programme delivery, stakeholder engagement, administration and communications; • monitoring programme delivery and performance against agreed milestones; and • providing progress reports, financial reporting and a final programme evaluation report in accordance with the requirements set out in Appendix 1 – Specification of Services.

title: Procurement of Sonosite LX Ultrasound System (Brand Name restriction)
description: Acquisition Description: This notice is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items using Simplified Acquisition Procedures. This acquisition will be made in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6 �Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and solicitation for commercial Items,� as applicable, and as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation (a written solicitation will not be issued) and quotes are being requested. This acquisition will be processed under FAR Part 13 Simplified Acquisition Procedures (SAP). The solicitation documents and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2024-04. The Solicitation number is RFQ-26-008281 and the solicitation is issued as a Request for Quotes (RFQ). Acquisition Description & Justification: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) Clinical Center requires the acquisition of a FUJIFILM Sonosite LX Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) System with multiple transducers to support pediatric critical care imaging. The system includes advanced diagnostic imaging capabilities, Color and Spectral Doppler, Tissue Harmonic Imaging, DICOM connectivity, wireless networking, integrated educational resources, manufacturer installation and training, and a five-year comprehensive warranty. The acquisition also includes specialty transducers to support cardiac, abdominal, pulmonary, vascular access, musculoskeletal, neonatal, and pediatric imaging applications. Justification: The Sonosite LX will provide clinicians with high-quality, real-time bedside imaging necessary for the care of critically ill pediatric patients in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU). The system supports rapid diagnosis and ultrasound-guided procedures, including vascular access, cardiac assessments, pulmonary evaluations, abdominal imaging, and other point-of-care applications. Its portability, exceptional image quality, intuitive touchscreen workflow, advanced needle visualization technology, and comprehensive imaging capabilities enable timely clinical decision-making, improve procedural success, reduce complications, and enhance patient safety. The inclusion of multiple transducers allows a single platform to support a broad range of pediatric and critical care examinations, maximizing clinical utility while minimizing equipment redundancy. The five-year manufacturer warranty and onsite clinical training further ensure long-term reliability and successful implementation. FUJIFILM Sonosite is a recognized industry leader in point-of-care ultrasound technology with extensive experience supporting hospitals and critical care environments. The vendor offers the complete Sonosite LX platform, manufacturer-certified installation, clinical education, technical support, and a comprehensive five-year warranty for both the ultrasound system and transducers. The proposed equipment is available through an existing federal contract, ensuring compliance with federal procurement requirements while providing access to factory-authorized service, software updates, replacement components, and ongoing technical support. As the original equipment manufacturer, FUJIFILM Sonosite is uniquely qualified to provide the equipment, warranty coverage, training, and lifecycle support necessary to maintain safe and reliable operation in the NIH Clinical Center's Pediatric Intensive Care Unit. Only this specific brand of equipment from Fujitsu Sonosite can be accepted. Vendors must be authorized resellers and provide their letter of authorization. description: Acquisition Description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) Clinical Center has a Rosa robot manufactured by Zimmer Biomet. This ROSA neurosurgical robot is capable of assisting endoscopic procedures and providing accurate localization and a robotic platform for performing deep brain stimulation surgery. The NIH requires a preventative maintenance agreement every year to ensure the robot is maintained in good condition and optimal performance. title: BIZON High-Performance Workstation PC
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. The Department of Health and Human Services intends to award a firm fixed price sole source contract under the authority of FAR Overhaul subpart 12.201-1, for purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT), Contracting Officers may solicit from only one source if the circumstances deem only one source is reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand name, or industrial mobilization). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334118 - Computer Terminal and Other Computer Peripheral Equipment Manufacturing, and the Product Service Code (PSC) is 7H20 � IT and Telecom � Platform Products: Database, Main. The purpose of this sole source award is to obtain a custom-configured enterprise-class Windows 11 Pro and NINDS IT compliant high-performance workstation to support big data multiparametric flow cytometry and multispectral image processing and analysis of multiplexed datasets sourced from whole specimen image scans of murine, monkey, and human brain tissue samples routinely acquired at the Flow Cytometry and Imaging Core Facility (FCICF) to support basic and clinical research within the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Market Research shows that only the Bizon G3000 has the essential characteristics and is compatible with the existing multiplex computational pipelines developed at FCICF. This synopsis does not constitute a solicitation, however interested parties may identify their interests and capability to respond to this requirement within five (5) calendar days of the publication of this notice. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to complete this procurement based upon response to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. No reimbursement for any cost connected with providing capability information will be provided. No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in the response to this notice. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Capability statements must be submitted by e-mail ONLY to john.alozie@hhs.gov no later than 10am (ET) on Monday, September 28, 2026, and reference Notice ID number PCA-NINDS-09192.

title: Security Clearance Processing
description: This is a sources sought notice for Market Research purposes ONLY. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. Responses in any form are not offers, and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. No funds are available to pay for the preparation of responses to this announcement. Information submitted is strictly voluntary. This information will be used to determine the availability of contractors capable of meeting the Government's minimum requirements. Telephone calls will not be accepted. Any questions regarding this notice shall be submitted in writing. Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Fleet Logistics Center Jacksonville (FLCJ) is seeking sources to determine if there are potentially qualified U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) certified 8(a), Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), HUBZone Small Business, Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB), and/or Small Business (SB) that are capable of providing Security Administration Support Services as described in the attached DRAFT Performance Work Statement. Requirement: The Commander, Patrol and Reconnaissance Wing Eleven (CPRW-11) requires contractor services to provide professional, administrative, and technical support for the CPRW-11 Special Security Office (SSO), Intelligence Directorate (N2), and security professionals throughout the CPRW-11. The contractor must perform a range of administrative security support functions, including processing security clearances, managing personnel security records in DISS, providing helpdesk support, and supporting security programs. Place of Performance: Work will be performed primarily at the N2 offices of CPRW-11 located in Jacksonville, Florida. NAICS Code: The potential North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) is 541611 - Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services. Submission Requirements: Interested sources are invited to respond to this sources sought announcement by submitting the following: Contractor Information: Provide your company name, address, POC name, phone number, email, CAGE code, UEI number, and NAICS. Size of Business: Large Business or Small Business. If small, please provide the socioeconomic status (e.g., 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone). Contract Vehicle: State if the services can be solicited from a General Services Administration (GSA) schedule contract vehicle or if they must be open-market. Capability Statement: A brief description of your company's capability, resources, technical competencies, and organizational experience relative to the key task areas in the PWS. Standard brochures and/or paraphrasing of the Draft PWS will not be considered sufficient to demonstrate capabilities. The statement must also address your company's ability to provide personnel who meet and can maintain eligibility for Favorable SCI � ICD 704 security clearance at the time of contract start. Those firms interested in providing information in response to this sources sought are requested to provide the above information by 10 A.M. EASTERN, Monday, September 28th, 2026. Submissions shall be sent via e-mail to Tristan McElhinney and Harold Melton at tristan.s.mcelhinney.civ@us.navy.mil and harold.m.melton.civ@us.navy.mil, respectively. The subject line of the e-mail shall read: Security Administration Support - Sources Sought. Submissions shall not exceed five single-sided pages in length. Disclaimer and Important Note: This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information submitted. Confidentiality: No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response. The Government reserves the right to use any non-proprietary technical information in any resultant solicitation(s).

title: F-16 CATALYST IRIDIUM SURPLUS
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP). THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT PAY FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH RESPONDING TO THIS SYNOPSIS. This sources sought / pre-solicitation notice is being issued by AFSC/PZACB, Hill AFB, UT, ahead of an anticipated urgent sole-source commercial supply buy for 12 ea surplus F-16 Iridium Catalyst. Due to unusual and compelling urgency, the Air Force requires delivery of this critical flight-safety asset no later than November 1, 2026, to prevent grounding of aircraft. The OEM, Honeywell International Inc. (CAGE 70210), is the sole manufacturer of newly produced catalyst but has a minimum production lead time of 328 days, rendering them unable to meet this urgent delivery schedule. Market research indicates that only a single qualified surplus supplier is in possession of an existing surplus lot of 12 ea catalyst that can meet this urgent delivery requirement. Therefore, the Government anticipates a single sole-source award to a qualified surplus supplier to secure these surplus parts. The Government does not own the rights to the data for the F-16 Catalyst Iridium. Honeywell possesses the proprietary data rights to this part. Any alternative interested sources must provide certified proof of qualified surplus inventory and demonstrate the absolute capability to deliver the exact NSN/PN on-site no later than November 1, 2026. Notice to Offeror(s)/Supplier(s): Funds are not presently available for this contract. The Government�s obligation under this contract is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds from which payment for contract purposes can be made. No legal liability on the part of the Government for any payment may arise until funds are made available to the Contracting Officer for this contract and until the Contractor receives notice of such availability, to be confirmed in writing by the Contracting Officer.

description: AMENDMENT 0001 � SEPTEMBER 25, 2026 The purpose of Amendment 0001 is to provide the Government�s consolidated responses to industry questions received in response to RFQ OMAS-01-2026, HHS Modernization Discovery, Prototyping, and Implementation Planning. Amendment 0001 also clarifies certain solicitation instructions and administrative matters. The quotation due date remains September 28, 2026 at 10:00 AM Eastern Time. Quoters that submitted a quotation before issuance of Amendment 0001 may either submit a revised quotation by the quotation deadline or provide written acknowledgment that their previously submitted quotation remains unchanged and is based on the solicitation as amended by Amendment 0001. If a revised quotation is submitted, the latest complete quotation received by the deadline will supersede the prior submission. Quoters are responsible for reviewing Amendment 0001 and the consolidated Government Questions and Answers attached to this notice. Attachment Added: Amendment 0001 � Consolidated Industry Questions and Government Responses Except as expressly clarified or revised by Amendment 0001, all other solicitation terms and conditions remain unchanged. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Office of the Assistant Secretary for Administration (ASA), Immediate Office (IO), is issuing this competitive Request for Quotations (RFQ) as a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside for a senior-led modernization discovery, prototyping, and implementation-planning engagement. This competitive RFQ follows the earlier FY26-ASA Notice of Intent. Market research and responses to that notice demonstrated a competitive small-business market. A response to the earlier notice is not, by itself, a quotation under this RFQ. Firms that responded to the earlier notice may incorporate specific unchanged capability information by reference as described in the attached RFQ. The anticipated 25-week engagement consists of a five-week Mobilization and Readiness Phase followed by a 20-week Discovery, Prototyping, and Implementation Planning Phase. Performance includes discovery interviews and working sessions; review of selected HHS workflows, systems, and technical operations; technical and process analysis; prioritization of modernization opportunities; development and testing of prototypes or proofs of concept; validation with HHS stakeholders; and preparation of implementation recommendations and plans. Required outputs include an integrated work plan, current-state assessment, prioritized modernization opportunities portfolio, technical recommendations, agreed prototypes or proofs of concept, implementation plans for HHS-selected opportunities/prototypes, supporting technical and operational documentation, an implementation roadmap, and an executive readout/summary. The attached RFQ contains the complete scope, quotation instructions, evaluation factors, pricing schedule, and applicable terms. HHS anticipates issuance of one firm-fixed-price purchase order. The Government intends to make award by September 30, 2026. QUOTATION SUBMISSION Submit quotations electronically to mesfin.alemayehu@hhs.gov no later than September 28, 2026 at 10:00 AM Eastern Time. Use the subject line: RFQ OMAS-01-2026 - [Company Name] - HHS Modernization. Questions are due September 25, 2026 at 10:00 AM Eastern Time to the same email address. Telephone quotations will not be accepted. Only eligible small business concerns under NAICS 541512 will be considered for award. Quoters must follow the attached RFQ instructions. ATTACHMENT 1. title: Water Intake Facility at Radford Army Ammunition Plant
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice for informational purposes only to determine the interest and availability of potential qualified contractors for a new Water Intake Facility at the Radford Army Ammuntion Plant (RFAAP). RFAAP, located in Radford, VA is a Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) production facility providing state-of-the-art propellants, energetics, and munitions to support the Warfighter. All production at RFAAP depends on river water. Completing construction to the supporting infrastructure and in-water work will ensure the continued operation of the primary water intake at RFAAP and resilience of water supply to the facility.

title: Security Clearance Processing
description: This is a sources sought notice for Market Research purposes ONLY. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. Responses in any form are not offers, and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. No funds are available to pay for the preparation of responses to this announcement. Information submitted is strictly voluntary. This information will be used to determine the availability of contractors capable of meeting the Government's minimum requirements. Telephone calls will not be accepted. Any questions regarding this notice shall be submitted in writing. Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Fleet Logistics Center Jacksonville (FLCJ) is seeking sources to determine if there are potentially qualified U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) certified 8(a), Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), HUBZone Small Business, Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB), and/or Small Business (SB) that are capable of providing Security Administration Support Services as described in the attached DRAFT Performance Work Statement. Requirement: The Commander, Patrol and Reconnaissance Wing Eleven (CPRW-11) requires contractor services to provide professional, administrative, and technical support for the CPRW-11 Special Security Office (SSO), Intelligence Directorate (N2), and security professionals throughout the CPRW-11. The contractor must perform a range of administrative security support functions, including processing security clearances, managing personnel security records in DISS, providing helpdesk support, and supporting security programs. Place of Performance: Work will be performed primarily at the N2 offices of CPRW-11 located in Jacksonville, Florida. NAICS Code: The potential North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) is 541611 - Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services. Submission Requirements: Interested sources are invited to respond to this sources sought announcement by submitting the following: Contractor Information: Provide your company name, address, POC name, phone number, email, CAGE code, UEI number, and NAICS. Size of Business: Large Business or Small Business. If small, please provide the socioeconomic status (e.g., 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone). Contract Vehicle: State if the services can be solicited from a General Services Administration (GSA) schedule contract vehicle or if they must be open-market. Capability Statement: A brief description of your company's capability, resources, technical competencies, and organizational experience relative to the key task areas in the PWS. Standard brochures and/or paraphrasing of the Draft PWS will not be considered sufficient to demonstrate capabilities. The statement must also address your company's ability to provide personnel who meet and can maintain eligibility for Favorable SCI � ICD 704 security clearance at the time of contract start. Those firms interested in providing information in response to this sources sought are requested to provide the above information by 1400 P.M. EASTERN, Friday, October 2nd, 2026. Submissions shall be sent via e-mail to Tristan McElhinney and Harold Melton at tristan.s.mcelhinney.civ@us.navy.mil and harold.m.melton.civ@us.navy.mil, respectively. The subject line of the e-mail shall read: Security Administration Support - Sources Sought. Submissions shall not exceed five single-sided pages in length. Disclaimer and Important Note: This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information submitted. Confidentiality: No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response. The Government reserves the right to use any non-proprietary technical information in any resultant solicitation(s).

title: Minot Air Force Base Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC) IDIQ
description: This is a Request for Proposal (RFP) for commercial, non-personal services prepared in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 "Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services", Part 15 "Contracting by Negotiation", and Part 36 "Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts" procedures. This acquisition is 100% set aside for Small Business Concerns. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code associated with this requirement is 236220 "Commercial and Institutional Building Construction". The Small Business Size Standard associated with this NAICS is $45,000,000.00. The 5th Contracting Squadron, Minot Air Force Base (AFB), North Dakota, is requesting proposals to establish the base award(s) for a Minot AFB Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC), Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) vehicle. The MACC IDIQ will fulfill a continuous and recurring need for a broad range of design-bid-build and design-build construction projects to support the missions of the 5th Bomb Wing, 91st Missile Wing, and multiple tenant units assigned to Minot AFB. There is no seed project included with this solicitation. The MACC will have an initial five (5)-year ordering period with one (1), five (5)-year optional ordering period. The total aggregate maximum amount expendable under the entire MACC lifecycle SHALL NOT EXCEED $500,000,000.00. The guaranteed minimum amount over the life of the MACC is $500.00. The awardees' guaranteed minimum will be satisfied by attendance at the MACC Post-Award Conference. NOTICE TO OFFERORS (AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS): Funds are not available for the minimum guarantee. Award under this solicitation is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds from which payment for contract purposes can be made. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any time. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse an offeror for any costs. The complete solicitation package is available in this posting. Anyone wishing to participate in this proposed procurement must obtain their copy from this website. Copies will not be distributed from the Contracting Office. All amendments will be posted on SAM.gov. Contractors are solely responsible for obtaining amendments from this site to update files. The complete solicitation package includes eight (8) attachments: 1. MACC Statement of Work 2. MACC Ordering Guide 3. MACC Specifications 4. Section L - Instructions to Offerors 5. Section M - Evaluation Factors for Award 6. Davis-Bacon Act Wage Determinations 7. Financial Responsibility Authorization Letter 8. Subcontractor Consent Letter NOTICE TO OFFERORS (MANDATORY SAM REGISTRATION): All prospective contractors must be registered and active in the System for Award Management (SAM) at time of receipt of proposals. Failure to be active and registered in SAM will cause your firm to be ineligible for award. Offerors are highly encouraged to thoroughly review all solicitation documents prior to submitting their proposal. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by the agency. All contractors� questions in response to this solicitation must be emailed to 5CONS.PKA-C.MACC@us.af.mil no later than 31 August 2026 at 10:00 AM CDT. The Government will not be held responsible for answering any questions after this time. All questions/answers resulting from this solicitation will be posted to SAM.gov as an amendment.

title: HHS Modernization Discovery, Prototyping, and Implementation Planning
description: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Office of the Assistant Secretary for Administration (ASA), Immediate Office (IO), is issuing this competitive Request for Quotations (RFQ) as a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside for a senior-led modernization discovery, prototyping, and implementation-planning engagement. This competitive RFQ follows the earlier FY26-ASA Notice of Intent. Market research and responses to that notice demonstrated a competitive small-business market. A response to the earlier notice is not, by itself, a quotation under this RFQ. Firms that responded to the earlier notice may incorporate specific unchanged capability information by reference as described in the attached RFQ. The anticipated 25-week engagement consists of a five-week Mobilization and Readiness Phase followed by a 20-week Discovery, Prototyping, and Implementation Planning Phase. Performance includes discovery interviews and working sessions; review of selected HHS workflows, systems, and technical operations; technical and process analysis; prioritization of modernization opportunities; development and testing of prototypes or proofs of concept; validation with HHS stakeholders; and preparation of implementation recommendations and plans. Required outputs include an integrated work plan, current-state assessment, prioritized modernization opportunities portfolio, technical recommendations, agreed prototypes or proofs of concept, implementation plans for HHS-selected opportunities/prototypes, supporting technical and operational documentation, an implementation roadmap, and an executive readout/summary. The attached RFQ contains the complete scope, quotation instructions, evaluation factors, pricing schedule, and applicable terms. HHS anticipates issuance of one firm-fixed-price purchase order. The Government intends to make award by September 30, 2026. QUOTATION SUBMISSION Submit quotations electronically to mesfin.alemayehu@hhs.gov no later than September 28, 2026 at 10:00 AM Eastern Time. Use the subject line: RFQ OMAS-01-2026 - [Company Name] - HHS Modernization. Questions are due September 25, 2026 at 10:00 AM Eastern Time to the same email address. Telephone quotations will not be accepted. Only eligible small business concerns under NAICS 541512 will be considered for award. Quoters must follow the attached RFQ instructions. ATTACHMENT 1. RFQ OMAS-01-2026 - HHS Modernization Discovery, Prototyping, and Implementation Planning

title: Service d'intervention d'urgence en cas de déversements accidentels et de récupération de contaminants
Netherlands – Endangered species protection services – Opstellen Soortenmanagementplan (SMP) Gemeente Hulst
description: Het onderzoeksgebied bestaat in beginsel uit bebouwing binnen de komgrenzen van de gemeente Hulst. Naast reguliere woonbebouwing dienen bijzondere objecten binnen of direct grenzend aan deze komgrenzen expliciet te worden beschouwd, waarbij onderbouwd wordt welke objecten ecologisch relevant zijn en welke onderzoeksinspanning passend is. De opdracht omvat naar verwachting onder meer: • bureauonderzoek en gegevensinventarisatie; • gebiedsdekkende quickscan; • soortgericht ecologisch onderzoek en nulmeting; • analyse van beschermde gebouwbewonende soorten; • effectbepaling; • opstellen van een concept en definitief SMP; • mitigatie- en compensatiestrategie; • monitorings- en evaluatieplan; • proces-, administratie- en managementplan; • GIS-dataset, kaartlagen, metadata en dataoverdracht; • afstemming met overheden De opdrachtnemer is verantwoordelijk voor de samenhang tussen onderzoek, analyse, effectbepaling, planvorming, vergunningaanvraag, GIS-data, monitoring en overdracht Als voorbereiding op het veldwerk en het opstellen van het soortenmanagementplan wordt er een gebiedsbrede quickscan uitgevoerd. Op basis van de quickscan wordt vastgesteld of gebiedsuitbreiding noodzakelijk is en of er diersoorten worden toegevoegd aan het onderzoek. Uitbreiding van gebieden en soorten vindt plaats in overleg met gemeente Hulst. Onderzoeksgebied Het primaire onderzoeksgebied bestaat uit de bebouwde kommen binnen de gemeente Hulst, zoals voorlopig weergegeven op de door Gemeente Hulst aangeleverde conceptkaart “Komgrenzen gemeente Hulst”. Deze begrenzing is nog niet definitief en kan voorafgaand aan publicatie van de aanbesteding worden aangepast of nader worden gespecificeerd. Het buitengebied behoort niet tot de primaire scope, tenzij aanvullend onderzoek buiten de komgrenzen ecologisch of vergunningtechnisch noodzakelijk blijkt voor een vergunningwaardige onderbouwing van het SMP. Naast reguliere woonbebouwing dienen inschrijvers in hun onderzoeksstrategie expliciet rekening te houden met bijzondere objecten binnen of direct grenzend aan de voorlopige komgrenzen. Daarbij kan onder meer worden gedacht aan kerken, kapellen, monumenten, gemeentelijk vastgoed, maatschappelijk vastgoed, scholen, sportaccommodaties, zorgvastgoed, appartementencomplexen, hoogbouw, begraafplaatsgebouwen, molens, torens, oude nutsgebouwen en overige ecologisch relevante gebouwen. Deze bijzondere objecten worden niet op voorhand allemaal als volledig onderzoeksplichtig aangemerkt. Van de toekomstige opdrachtnemer wordt verwacht dat hij in de onderzoeksstrategie onderbouwt welke objecten ecologisch relevant zijn, welke onderzoeksinspanning daarbij passend is en hoe wordt voorkomen dat relevante verblijfplaatsen, kraamlocaties, massawinterverblijven, nestplaatsen of functionele leefgebieden buiten beeld blijven. De definitieve onderzoeksbegrenzing, objectcategorieën en eventuele objectenlijst worden vastgesteld in de aanbestedingsstukken. Gebouwbewonende beschermde soorten Minimaal worden er in het onderzoek de gebouwbewonenden vleermuizen, de gierzwaluw, de huismus, huiszwaluw en de steenmarter (mogelijk alleen als indicatiesoort) meegenomen. Op basis van de quickscan is eventuele uitbreiding mogelijk.

title: SourcesSought_BaseWideFurnitureMaintenance2026
description: SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS (Not a Notice of Solicitation) DESCRIPTION: Notice from the United States Air Force, Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Operational Contacting Division, Base Support Contracting Branch at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), Ohio: INTRODUCTION - The AFLCMC Operational Contracting Branch at Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio, on behalf of the 88th Civil Engineer Group, is conducting market research through a Sources Sought Notice to identify potential sources, including Small Businesses (SB), capable of providing Base-Wide Furniture Maintenance (BWFM), telecommunications, and minor interior finishing support at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), Ohio. This notice is for informational purposes only to determine the availability of qualified sources to support this requirement. A set-aside decision has not yet been made for this acquisition. Requirements: The 88th Civil Engineer Group (88 CEG) requires a contractor to provide all personnel, equipment, tools, and materials necessary to perform furniture maintenance, redesign, installation, and associated support services. The scope of work includes, but is not limited to, the following core requirements: Furniture Maintenance & Installation: Disassembly, reconfiguration, and installation of various systems furniture (e.g., Herman Miller, Steelcase, Haworth, Knoll). Computer-Aided Design (CAD): Providing 2D and 3D layout designs and Labor & Material (L&M) quotes. Warehousing & Inventory Management: Managing and conducting inventory of Government-owned furniture assets within a Government-furnished, on-site warehouse facility. Telecommunications & Data Cabling: Coordinating and executing the routing of communication lines through furniture, including adherence to WPAFB standards for CAT6 and non-CAT6 cabling. Ancillary Interior Services: Providing minor interior finishing services incidental to furniture reconfiguration, which may include patching/painting, minor plumbing, and electrical adjustments as required. Safeguarding Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI): Adhering to strict policies for handling and storing facility floor plans. CAPABILITY STATEMENT REQUIREMENTS Interested parties are requested to submit a Capability Statement (no more than 7 pages). The statement must address the contractor�s ability to perform the tasks outlined in the Scope of Work. Please include: Company Profile: Company name, address, POC, CAGE Code, UEI number, and socioeconomic status. Furniture & Design Expertise: A summary of experience with multi-manufacturer systems furniture and providing CAD layouts. Warehouse & Inventory Management: Your approach to managing a Government-furnished warehouse and inventory. Telecommunications & Ancillary Services (CRITICAL): A detailed explanation of how your company will execute the data cabling, electrical, plumbing, and painting requirements. Please specify whether this work will be performed by in-house technicians or through subcontracting/teaming agreements. Security Clearances: Confirmation of the ability to meet CUI safeguarding and base access requirements. Closing: RESPONSES ARE DUE NOT LATER THAN 28 September 2026 BY 10:30 AM EDT. Direct all questions concerning this acquisition to alisha.cvitkovich@us.af.mil. Responses may be submitted electronically to the following e-mail address: alisha.cvitkovich@us.af.mil and andrew.petersen.3@us.af.mil. All correspondence sent via email shall contain a subject line that reads "Base Wide Furniture Maintenance Follow-On." This is a Sources Sought notice for market research purposes only. In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overall (RFO) 15.101, responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Any information submitted by respondents to this notice is strictly voluntary and will not be reimbursed by the Government. The Government�s assessment of the capability statements received will factor in whether any forthcoming solicitation will be conducted as a full and open competition or as a set-aside. Attachments: Draft PWS Base Wide Furniture Maintenance 20 July 2026 Sources Sought Synopsis

title: Ireland – Radio, television, communication, telecommunication and related equipment – Containerised Communications Solutions
description: The Defence Forces have a requirement to procure a quantity of Containerised Communications solutions over the next 5 years. The purpose of these containers is to provide a mobile communications centre / office space which will be used to support Defence Forces operational deployments in the field. The containers will be mounted to an existing fleet of 4 x 4 trucks which will potentially change over time. To account for the changing nature of vehicle platforms the containers must be of a standard 20 Foot ISO (TEU) design complete with standard ISO corner casting / twist lock fitting to enable the rapid changing, mounting, demounting and movement via other means etc. When deployed the container must be capable to providing a shared work space for a minimum of 3 x communications operatives and capable of housing/running/sustaining a wide array of communications services in the field for up to 96 hours. The attached documents outlines the Mandatory Requirements (MR) and Optional Requirements (OR) for each of the individual Lots.

title: Corning and Holt 10 Levee Repairs
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District, is issuing a solicitation and awarding a single contract for construction services for levee repair at Corning and Holt 10 Levees, located in Holt County, Missouri. title: X1LZ--Center Mall Parking - NWI (VA-26-00085491)
description: This is a Notice of Intent published in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 5.101(a)(1) requiring the dissemination of information regarding proposed contract actions. The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 23, intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to The Center, LLC under FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i), Only One Source Reasonably Available. The requirement is for 199 parking spaces within a five-minute walking distance of the Omaha VA Medical Center. The Omaha VA currently utilizes parking spaces at The Center Mall. Based on market research, The Center, LLC is the only reasonable available source with sufficient parking capacity to provide 199 spaces within the required five-minute walking distance. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 81290 Parking Lots and Garages, and the Product Service Code (PSC) is X1LZ lease/Rental of Parking Facilities. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government s requirement may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide 199 parking spaces within a five-minute walking distance of the Omaha VA Medical Center. title: Airfield Civil Works IDIQ
description: This is the official solicitation for the Tyndall Air Force Base Airfield Civil Works Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) requirement. The points of contact (POCs) for this pre-solicitation are SrA Frances Montgomery at (850)283-8640 or frances.motngomery@us.af.mil, Mr. Joseph Petersen at (850)283-8618 or joseph.petersen.3@us.af.mil, and Mrs. Tanya Gutka at (850)283-8650 or tanya.gutka@us.af.mil. This will be a 100% Small Business Set-Aside under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 237310 Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction and the Product Service Code (PSC) Z2BD Repair or Alteration of Airport Runways and Taxiways Services. The small business size standard under NAICS 237310 is $45,000,000.00. The Department of the Air Force anticipates issuing a solicitation for a comprehensive Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to execute various civil works projects on the active airfield at Tyndall AFB where specific requirements and quantities will be established via individual Task Orders throughout the five-year ordering period (base year and four option years). The scope of work encompasses the demolition, repair, and new construction of heavy-load airfield pavements, including Portland Cement Concrete (PCC), Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA), and interlocking pavers. Associated civil infrastructure tasks include earthwork, subgrade preparation, and grading. Key Operational and Environmental Constraints: This requirement necessitates operating within a highly restricted, active military flightline environment. The successful contractor must possess the proven capability to: Execute complex construction phasing that minimizes operational downtime for active runways and taxiways; maintain rigorous flightline safety protocols; including comprehensive Foreign Object Debris (FOD) prevention and dynamic coordination with Air Traffic Control (ATC) and Airfield Management; achieve strict adherence to Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) for heavy aircraft loading and DoD safety manual EM 385-1-1; manage complex environmental compliance; including securing Environmental Resource Permits (ERP) and safely handling, containing, and disposing of contaminated soils and groundwater, specifically in areas impacted by Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF). All potential offerors will submit proposals through the PIEE Solicitation module. Proposals are due NLT 05 OCT 26 at 09:30 AM CDT. Questions are due NLT 08 SEP 26 at 10:00 AM CDT.

As a result, no other vendors or technicians are authorized or technically capable of performing maintenance or repairs on this instrument, nor can they obtain the necessary parts to service or replace malfunctioning components. Because of these restrictions, only Wildlife Dominion can provide qualified technical support, authorized repairs, and genuine replacement parts for the HogEye Cellular Camera Systems. These instruments are crucial to the operational activities of Wildlife Services (WS). Improper maintenance or unauthorized repairs would risk equipment failure, work stoppages, and significant additional costs associated with restoring or replacing the instrument. (4) Identify the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition. The statutory authority supporting the placement of an order or establishment of a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) that exceeds the micro-purchase threshold on a sole source basis is: FAR 16.507-7 - Items Peculiar to One Manufacturer (5) Demonstrate that the proposed contractor's unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires using the authority cited. The Wildlife Dominion HOGEYE Cellular Camera Systems possesses unique capabilities not available in other commercially available camera systems. Wildlife Dominion�s integration of hardware/software allows for the remote trigging of propane cannons (and optional pyrotechnic launchers) from the camera interface. This feature is essential to the USDA�s ongoing, non-lethal harassment of piscivorous bird species to mitigate depredation to aquaculture facilities. No other manufacturer offers a spectrometer with identical calibration technology, analytical algorithms, or output compatibility. Competing instruments lack one or more of the following required capabilities: Solar-powered cellular camera system with infrared night vision and motion-triggered detection. Real-time alerts with image/video capture sent via cellular LTE network. Rugged, weatherproof design for field deployment in aquaculture environments. Integrated remote-control unit allowing linkage with deterrent devices (e.g., propane cannons, pyrotechnic launchers). Remote arming/disarming capability through secure app interface. Capable of sustained autonomous field operation without daily maintenance. Live video. Cellular-enabled camera systems. Propane scare cannons. Remote cannon detonation. (6) A determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable. The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost to the Government of the supplies/services covered by this J&A will be fair and reasonable based on a thorough comparison of historical pricing data from the prior contract and the development of an Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE) using current market rates. (7) A description of the market research conducted, and the results or a statement of the reason Market Research was not conducted. Market research was conducted to verify the availability of comparable cellular camera systems from other vendors. The findings confirmed that no other cellular camera systems met our required compatibility and performance criteria. All responsible sources may submit a response which will be considered by the agency. Please email responses to Jeanine Goral Jeanine.J.Goral@usda.gov. no later than the response date of this notice. Telephonic inquiries will not be honored.

title: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement
description: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement. USACE, Pittsburgh District, has an upcoming requirement to replace the siding of the Resource Managers Office at Youghiogheny River Lake. The work described herein shall be performed at the Youghiogheny Resource Managers Office (RMO) building located within the Youghiogheny River Lake project area in Confluence, Pennsylvania. The building currently serves as administrative office space for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The RMO building was constructed in 1986 and is a multi-level, timber-framed structure built into the hillside overlooking the impoundment side of the dam. The exterior walls consist of 2x6 wood stud framing with 6-inch fiberglass batt insulation (R-19, foil-faced). Interior partitions consist of 2x4 wood studs with 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard. The existing exterior wall assembly consists of 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing with 5/8-inch cedar-faced T1-11 plywood siding, for a combined nominal thickness of 1-1/8 inches. Exterior trim and fascia consist of various widths of cedar lumber. The building is supported by cast-in-place concrete footings and 12-inch concrete masonry unit (CMU) foundation walls. The rear wall section and balcony framing are supported by 4 feet-0 inches wide by 5 feet-0 inches deep concrete footings, laminated wood columns (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches), and laminated wood beams (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches).This project consists of the removal and replacement of the existing exterior wall cladding system. The Contractor shall remove and dispose of the existing T1-11 siding and 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing in their entirety. The Contractor shall furnish and install a new exterior wall assembly consisting of 1/2-inch APA-rated structural wood sheathing, a continuous weather-resistive barrier (WRB), 3/8-inch nominal preservative-treated wood furring strips, and 5/16-inch fiber cement lap siding in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The new wall assembly is intended to match the existing wall thickness (approximately 1-1/8 inches) to maintain alignment with existing window and door openings. Minor dimensional variation within normal construction tolerances are acceptable and shall not require modification or resetting of existing windows and doors. The Contractor shall not reset, relocate, or otherwise modify existing windows and doors. Furring strips shall be installed vertically over the WRB at a maximum spacing of 16 inches on center and shall be fastened through the sheathing into wall framing members. Fiber cement siding shall be installed horizontally over the furring strips and fastened through the furring and sheathing into wall framing members. Furring strips are intended to provide a drainage and ventilation cavity and shall not be used as the sole fastening substrate for the fiber cement lap siding. The Contractor shall ensure that all fiber cement lap siding edges are supported by framing members or approved blocking in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The Contractor shall furnish and install all required trim at windows, doors, corners, and transitions. Trim material shall be fiber cement. The cedar hand railing on the balconys is to be new capped PVC or capped composite decking of matching color to fiber cement board siding. The Contractor shall provide complete flashing at all required locations, including but not limited to head flashing at windows and doors, Z-flashing at horizontal joints and transitions, and kick-out flashing at roof-to-wall intersections. All flashing shall be integrated with the WRB in a shingle-lap manner to maintain a continuous drainage plane. The work shall be completed within 180 after written Notice to Proceed. The points of contact (POCs) for this pre-solicitation are SrA Frances Montgomery at (850)283-8640 or frances.motngomery@us.af.mil, Mr. Joseph Petersen at (850)283-8618 or joseph.petersen.3@us.af.mil, and Mrs. Tanya Gutka at (850)283-8650 or tanya.gutka@us.af.mil. This will be a 100% Small Business Set-Aside under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 237310 Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction and the Product Service Code (PSC) Z2BD Repair or Alteration of Airport Runways and Taxiways Services. The small business size standard under NAICS 237310 is $45,000,000.00. The Department of the Air Force anticipates issuing a solicitation for a comprehensive Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to execute various civil works projects on the active airfield at Tyndall AFB where specific requirements and quantities will be established via individual Task Orders throughout the five-year ordering period (base year and four option years). Associated civil infrastructure tasks include earthwork, subgrade preparation, and grading. Key Operational and Environmental Constraints: This requirement necessitates operating within a highly restricted, active military flightline environment. The successful contractor must possess the proven capability to: Execute complex construction phasing that minimizes operational downtime for active runways and taxiways; maintain rigorous flightline safety protocols; including comprehensive Foreign Object Debris (FOD) prevention and dynamic coordination with Air Traffic Control (ATC) and Airfield Management; achieve strict adherence to Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) for heavy aircraft loading and DoD safety manual EM 385-1-1; manage complex environmental compliance; including securing Environmental Resource Permits (ERP) and safely handling, containing, and disposing of contaminated soils and groundwater, specifically in areas impacted by Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF). title: Airfield Civil Works IDIQ
description: This is the official solicitation for the Tyndall Air Force Base Airfield Civil Works Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) requirement. The points of contact (POCs) for this pre-solicitation are SrA Frances Montgomery at (850)283-8640 or frances.motngomery@us.af.mil, Mr. Joseph Petersen at (850)283-8618 or joseph.petersen.3@us.af.mil, and Mrs. Tanya Gutka at (850)283-8650 or tanya.gutka@us.af.mil. This will be a 100% Small Business Set-Aside under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 237310 Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction and the Product Service Code (PSC) Z2BD Repair or Alteration of Airport Runways and Taxiways Services. The small business size standard under NAICS 237310 is $45,000,000.00. The Department of the Air Force anticipates issuing a solicitation for a comprehensive Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to execute various civil works projects on the active airfield at Tyndall AFB where specific requirements and quantities will be established via individual Task Orders throughout the five-year ordering period (base year and four option years). The scope of work encompasses the demolition, repair, and new construction of heavy-load airfield pavements, including Portland Cement Concrete (PCC), Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA), and interlocking pavers. Associated civil infrastructure tasks include earthwork, subgrade preparation, and grading. Key Operational and Environmental Constraints: This requirement necessitates operating within a highly restricted, active military flightline environment. The successful contractor must possess the proven capability to: Execute complex construction phasing that minimizes operational downtime for active runways and taxiways; maintain rigorous flightline safety protocols; including comprehensive Foreign Object Debris (FOD) prevention and dynamic coordination with Air Traffic Control (ATC) and Airfield Management; achieve strict adherence to Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) for heavy aircraft loading and DoD safety manual EM 385-1-1; manage complex environmental compliance; including securing Environmental Resource Permits (ERP) and safely handling, containing, and disposing of contaminated soils and groundwater, specifically in areas impacted by Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF). All potential offerors will submit proposals through the PIEE Solicitation module. Proposals are due NLT 28 SEP 26 at 10:00 AM CDT. Questions are due NLT 08 SEP 26 at 10:00 AM CDT.

title: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement
description: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement. USACE, Pittsburgh District, has an upcoming requirement to replace the siding of the Resource Managers Office at Youghiogheny River Lake. The work described herein shall be performed at the Youghiogheny Resource Managers Office (RMO) building located within the Youghiogheny River Lake project area in Confluence, Pennsylvania. The building currently serves as administrative office space for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The RMO building was constructed in 1986 and is a multi-level, timber-framed structure built into the hillside overlooking the impoundment side of the dam. The exterior walls consist of 2x6 wood stud framing with 6-inch fiberglass batt insulation (R-19, foil-faced). Interior partitions consist of 2x4 wood studs with 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard. The existing exterior wall assembly consists of 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing with 5/8-inch cedar-faced T1-11 plywood siding, for a combined nominal thickness of 1-1/8 inches. Exterior trim and fascia consist of various widths of cedar lumber. The building is supported by cast-in-place concrete footings and 12-inch concrete masonry unit (CMU) foundation walls. The rear wall section and balcony framing are supported by 4 feet-0 inches wide by 5 feet-0 inches deep concrete footings, laminated wood columns (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches), and laminated wood beams (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches).This project consists of the removal and replacement of the existing exterior wall cladding system. The Contractor shall remove and dispose of the existing T1-11 siding and 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing in their entirety. The Contractor shall furnish and install a new exterior wall assembly consisting of 1/2-inch APA-rated structural wood sheathing, a continuous weather-resistive barrier (WRB), 3/8-inch nominal preservative-treated wood furring strips, and 5/16-inch fiber cement lap siding in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The new wall assembly is intended to match the existing wall thickness (approximately 1-1/8 inches) to maintain alignment with existing window and door openings. Minor dimensional variation within normal construction tolerances are acceptable and shall not require modification or resetting of existing windows and doors. The Contractor shall not reset, relocate, or otherwise modify existing windows and doors. Furring strips shall be installed vertically over the WRB at a maximum spacing of 16 inches on center and shall be fastened through the sheathing into wall framing members. Fiber cement siding shall be installed horizontally over the furring strips and fastened through the furring and sheathing into wall framing members. Furring strips are intended to provide a drainage and ventilation cavity and shall not be used as the sole fastening substrate for the fiber cement lap siding. The Contractor shall ensure that all fiber cement lap siding edges are supported by framing members or approved blocking in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The Contractor shall furnish and install all required trim at windows, doors, corners, and transitions. Trim material shall be fiber cement. The cedar hand railing on the balconys is to be new capped PVC or capped composite decking of matching color to fiber cement board siding. The Contractor shall provide complete flashing at all required locations, including but not limited to head flashing at windows and doors, Z-flashing at horizontal joints and transitions, and kick-out flashing at roof-to-wall intersections. All flashing shall be integrated with the WRB in a shingle-lap manner to maintain a continuous drainage plane. The work shall be completed within 180 after written Notice to Proceed. Disclosure of Magnitude of Construction (FAR 36.204 and DFARS 236.204) The acquisition will be procured as 100% Set-Aside for Small Business. The resulting award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract. All responsible Quoters are encouraged to participate. title: USCGC Healy Relief Valves Overhaul
description: STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) Vessel: USCGC HEALY (WAGB 20) Project: Relief Valves Overhaul 1.0 SCOPE Requirements for the inspection, overhaul, and testing of two (2) relief valves, Part Number: S8LJE-02RF1-03RF1-SS-H2-TB, belonging to the United States Coast Guard Cutter (USCGC) HEALY, homeported in Seattle, WA. Location: Contractor�s Facility. 2.0 BACKGROUND USCGC HEALY requires routine periodic maintenance and overhaul of mechanical systems to ensure operational readiness and safety. The specified relief valve requires a full overhaul, including the replacement of all soft goods, reassembly, and testing to restore it to Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) specifications. 3.0 REFERENCES The Contractor shall adhere to the following references during the performance of this work: 3.1 Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Technical Manuals and specifications for PN: S8LJE-02RF1-03RF1-SS-H2-TB. 3.2 U.S. Coast Guard Standard Specification (CG-47) - General Requirements for Ship Repair. 4.0 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS CLIN 001 The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, and facilities necessary to perform the following: 4.1 Disassembly and Cleaning ? Carefully disassemble the relief valve in accordance with OEM guidelines. ? Thoroughly clean all internal and external components to remove scale, debris, and marine growth without damaging the base metal or seating surfaces. ?4.2 Inspection ? Perform a visual and dimensional inspection of all hard parts (body, spring, stem, disc, nozzle, etc.). ? Identify any wear, pitting, scoring, or damage that exceeds OEM tolerances. ? Deliverable: Submit a Condition Found Report (CFR) to the Coast Guard Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) detailing the inspection results and recommending any additional repairs or replacement of hard parts prior to proceeding. 4.3 Overhaul and Reassembly ? Upon approval of the CFR, replace all soft goods (including O-rings, gaskets, packing, and seals) using 100% genuine OEM replacement parts. ? Machine or lap seating surfaces as necessary to achieve a proper seal, strictly within OEM tolerances. ? Reassemble the valve in accordance with OEM specifications, applying the correct torque values to all fasteners. 4.4 Testing and Calibration ? Perform hydrostatic shell testing and seat leakage testing in accordance with applicable OEM and industry standards. ? Set, calibrate, and pop-test the relief valve to the designated set pressure required by the ship's system parameters. ? A?ix a new metallic calibration tag to the valve indicating the set pressure, test date, and contractor identification. ? Deliverable: Provide a certified Test Report documenting the set pressure, pop pressure, reseat pressure, and confirmation of zero leakage. 5.0 GOVERNMENT FURNISHED PROPERTY (GFP) The Coast Guard will provide the following: ? Two (2) Relief Valve, PN: S8LJE-02RF1-03RF1-SS-H2-TB. USCG will ship valves to the contractor. Contractor is responsible for shipment of valves to USCG Base Seattle via two-day delivery methods. 6.0 Period of Performance: within 15 days from the award. 6.1 CLIN 0002: Potential Repairs based on CFR not to exceed ($1,500 dollars) 6.2. Pricing for any additional travel costs, material, or field service days will be requested and handled by the KO under the terms of the contract. Any repairs beyond the base scope identified because of the troubleshooting shall be documented in a Condition Found Report (CFR) with a technical description of the recommended repairs. The CFR shall be provided to the Technical POCs and the Contracting O?icer. 6.3. Any additional work will be authorized only by the KO through a written contract modification. The contractor shall not perform any repairs beyond the base scope until specifically authorized in writing by the KO. If the Government elects to proceed with additional repairs, the KO will issue a written contract modification that identifies the authorized additional work and associated firm fixed price. The contractor shall base any proposal for additional repairs on the findings in the CFR. For questions regarding this SOW contact: MKCM Armando Perez @ Armando.perez@uscg.mil

title: Schriever Cyber Threat Intelligence Software
description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Solicitation Number: FA255026Q0060 Notice Type: Presolicitation SOLICITATION TYPE: This is a sole source acquisition under RFO 6.103-1 (Only One Responsible Source) and 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) CONTRACTING OFFICE: Department of the Air Force 50th Contracting Squadron, PKB 210 Falcon Parkway, Suite 2116 Schriever Space Force Base, Colorado 80912 POINT OF CONTACT: Name: Alejandro Castellanos Email: alejandro.castellanos@spaceforce.mil Phone: 719-567-6185 NAICS CODE: 541511 NAICS SIZE STANDARD: $34M PRODUCT SERVICE CODE (PSC): DJ10 SET-ASIDE: None � Sole Source Acquisition DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT: The Department of the Air Force intends to award a sole source contract to Argonne Ridge Group, LLC for Augury Platinum software for Schriever Space Force Base. This requirement includes the following services: 1. Global Netflow Analytics & Threat Tracking Netflow Telemetry Querying: Provide access to a massive, global network flow database with the ability to run targeted queries on source/destination IP addresses, ports, protocol types, packet counts, and timestamps. Threat Infrastructure Tracking: Enable analysts to trace malicious command and control (C2) servers, map botnets, analyze hostile infrastructure, and perform forensic attribution. Passive DNS & IP Reputation: Integrated access to historical passive DNS databases and IP threat scores to quickly context-resolve suspect nodes. Encrypted Traffic Profiling: Capabilities to identify and analyze anomalous traffic patterns and identify threat actors utilizing virtual private networks (VPNs) or encrypted tunneling. 2. System Access & Seat Allocation License Tier: Platinum level subscription. User Capacity: 15 dedicated user licenses (seats) for cyber defense analysts. Secure, web-based software platform with 24/7/365 availability. API endpoints for integrating intelligence feeds directly into the unit's local security tools, Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems, or data orchestrators. 3. Operations & Maintenance Support Software Updates: Ongoing platform upgrades, database maintenance, search engine optimization, and feature additions throughout the performance periods at no extra cost. Technical Support: Helpdesk and administrator support for user troubleshooting, configuration assistance, and platform optimization. Up to three training sessions are available with Augury subscriptions. CONTRACT TYPE: Firm-Fixed-Price PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: Base Year: Sep 30, 2026 To Mar 29, 2027 Option Year 1: Mar 30, 2027 To Jun 29, 2027 Option Year 2: Jun 30, 2027 To Sep 29, 2027 Option Year 3: Sep 30, 2027 To Sep 29, 2028 Option Year 4: Sep 30, 2028 To Sep 29, 2029 SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION: This acquisition is proposed on a sole-source basis to Argonne Ridge Group, LLC, under the authority of RFO 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source, and 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1). Augury is currently integrated into Mission Delta 6�s operational baseline through prior work performed with U.S. Space Command. As a result, Augury represents the only known capability that is presently integrated and available to support the requirement without additional platform-validation, integration, security, and sustainment efforts. Award to Argonne Ridge Group, LLC would avoid the cost, schedule impact, and operational risk associated with modifying the current infrastructure; conducting additional demonstrations and security assessments; integrating a new platform; migrating data and workflows; and training personnel on a replacement capability. These additional efforts would delay fielding of a needed capability and introduce unnecessary cost and risk to the Government. A Sources Sought notice, FA255026AC002, was posted on SAM.gov on 21 September 2026 for three days to identify other software platforms capable of meeting the requirement. Although market research identified other potentially similar capabilities, the responses did not demonstrate that any alternative platform is immediately deployable and fully compliant with Mission Delta 6 requirements. Specifically, the alternative submissions contained unresolved gaps related to material capability validation, data sources and retention, integration methods, security boundaries, hosting, application programming interface specifications, service-level agreements, and sustainment. Further demonstrations, technical assessments, and integration efforts would be required before the Government could determine whether those platforms satisfy the requirement and can be integrated into Department of the Air Force Department of Defense Information Network systems. Argonne Ridge Group, LLC is the only known responsible source capable of providing the required Augury capability to meet the Government�s immediate operational need. ANTICIPATED SOLICITATION ISSUANCE DATE: On or about 28 Sep 2026. RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE: This is a presolicitation notice only. No quotes or proposals are being requested at this time. A solicitation will be issued directly to Argonne Ridge Group, LLC as the sole source contractor. This notice is being posted to satisfy the requirements of RFO 5.101 for acquisitions using the authority at RFO 6.103-1. Interested parties may submit capability statements or information relevant to this requirement; however, this is a sole source acquisition and the Government does not intend to award to any other contractor.

title: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement
description: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement. USACE, Pittsburgh District, has an upcoming requirement to replace the siding of the Resource Managers Office at Youghiogheny River Lake. The work described herein shall be performed at the Youghiogheny Resource Managers Office (RMO) building located within the Youghiogheny River Lake project area in Confluence, Pennsylvania. The building currently serves as administrative office space for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The RMO building was constructed in 1986 and is a multi-level, timber-framed structure built into the hillside overlooking the impoundment side of the dam. The exterior walls consist of 2x6 wood stud framing with 6-inch fiberglass batt insulation (R-19, foil-faced). Interior partitions consist of 2x4 wood studs with 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard. The existing exterior wall assembly consists of 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing with 5/8-inch cedar-faced T1-11 plywood siding, for a combined nominal thickness of 1-1/8 inches. Exterior trim and fascia consist of various widths of cedar lumber. The building is supported by cast-in-place concrete footings and 12-inch concrete masonry unit (CMU) foundation walls. The rear wall section and balcony framing are supported by 4 feet-0 inches wide by 5 feet-0 inches deep concrete footings, laminated wood columns (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches), and laminated wood beams (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches).This project consists of the removal and replacement of the existing exterior wall cladding system. The Contractor shall remove and dispose of the existing T1-11 siding and 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing in their entirety. The Contractor shall furnish and install a new exterior wall assembly consisting of 1/2-inch APA-rated structural wood sheathing, a continuous weather-resistive barrier (WRB), 3/8-inch nominal preservative-treated wood furring strips, and 5/16-inch fiber cement lap siding in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The new wall assembly is intended to match the existing wall thickness (approximately 1-1/8 inches) to maintain alignment with existing window and door openings. Minor dimensional variation within normal construction tolerances are acceptable and shall not require modification or resetting of existing windows and doors. The Contractor shall not reset, relocate, or otherwise modify existing windows and doors. Furring strips shall be installed vertically over the WRB at a maximum spacing of 16 inches on center and shall be fastened through the sheathing into wall framing members. Fiber cement siding shall be installed horizontally over the furring strips and fastened through the furring and sheathing into wall framing members. Furring strips are intended to provide a drainage and ventilation cavity and shall not be used as the sole fastening substrate for the fiber cement lap siding. The Contractor shall ensure that all fiber cement lap siding edges are supported by framing members or approved blocking in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The Contractor shall furnish and install all required trim at windows, doors, corners, and transitions. Trim material shall be fiber cement. The cedar hand railing on the balconys is to be new capped PVC or capped composite decking of matching color to fiber cement board siding. The Contractor shall provide complete flashing at all required locations, including but not limited to head flashing at windows and doors, Z-flashing at horizontal joints and transitions, and kick-out flashing at roof-to-wall intersections. All flashing shall be integrated with the WRB in a shingle-lap manner to maintain a continuous drainage plane. The work shall be completed within 180 after written Notice to Proceed. title: Airfield Civil Works IDIQ
description: This is the official solicitation for the Tyndall Air Force Base Airfield Civil Works Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) requirement. The points of contact (POCs) for this pre-solicitation are SrA Frances Montgomery at (850)283-8640 or frances.motngomery@us.af.mil, Mr. Joseph Petersen at (850)283-8618 or joseph.petersen.3@us.af.mil, and Mrs. Tanya Gutka at (850)283-8650 or tanya.gutka@us.af.mil. This will be a 100% Small Business Set-Aside under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 237310 Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction and the Product Service Code (PSC) Z2BD Repair or Alteration of Airport Runways and Taxiways Services. The small business size standard under NAICS 237310 is $45,000,000.00. The Department of the Air Force anticipates issuing a solicitation for a comprehensive Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to execute various civil works projects on the active airfield at Tyndall AFB where specific requirements and quantities will be established via individual Task Orders throughout the five-year ordering period (base year and four option years). The scope of work encompasses the demolition, repair, and new construction of heavy-load airfield pavements, including Portland Cement Concrete (PCC), Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA), and interlocking pavers. Associated civil infrastructure tasks include earthwork, subgrade preparation, and grading. Key Operational and Environmental Constraints: This requirement necessitates operating within a highly restricted, active military flightline environment. The successful contractor must possess the proven capability to: Execute complex construction phasing that minimizes operational downtime for active runways and taxiways; maintain rigorous flightline safety protocols; including comprehensive Foreign Object Debris (FOD) prevention and dynamic coordination with Air Traffic Control (ATC) and Airfield Management; achieve strict adherence to Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) for heavy aircraft loading and DoD safety manual EM 385-1-1; manage complex environmental compliance; including securing Environmental Resource Permits (ERP) and safely handling, containing, and disposing of contaminated soils and groundwater, specifically in areas impacted by Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF). All potential offerors will submit proposals through the PIEE Solicitation module. Proposals are due NLT 28 SEP 26 at 10:00 AM CDT. Questions are due NLT 08 SEP 26 at 10:00 AM CDT.
